sc: Toddler after a cold, barking cough, hoarse voice, worse at night → Croup: dexamethasone
Unvaccinated child, high fever, drooling, muffled voice, sits forward → Epiglottitis: secure the airway
Infant after a cold, ear pulling, red bulging drum → Otitis media: amoxicillin 5 days
f: Parainfluenza · 6 months–6 years · dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg single dose · stridor at rest: nebulised adrenaline 0.5 ml/kg 1:1000
Fever, exudate, tender nodes, no cough → strep · penicillin/amoxicillin 10 days (within 9 days prevents rheumatic fever)
S. pneumoniae · amoxicillin 5 days · glue ear: speech delay, flat tympanogram → grommets · mastoiditis → IV antibiotics
Croup · epiglottitis · foreign body · anaphylaxis · bacterial tracheitis · laryngomalacia (from birth) · subglottic stenosis
Peritonsillar abscess (trismus, uvula deviated) · mastoiditis · rheumatic fever · post-strep GN
Colds 6–8/year in a young child · ear discharge > 14 days = chronic · cold > 10 days → sinusitis
trap: Most sore throats are viral · amoxicillin in glandular fever → rash · a croup child who becomes quiet may be tiring · epiglottitis: do not examine the throat or lie the child down
